entries.title: Low curriculum w_focus and LR spikes cause catastrophic specification drift
entries.lesson: When w_focus is set too low (e.g., 0.1) during curriculum, the optimizer does not strongly constrain EFL, F-number, and FOV, allowing drift exceeding 300%. LR spikes in both curriculum and fine-tune phases (e.g., 0.0001→0.01, a 100× increase) amplify this drift. Once drift exceeds ~100%, fine-tuning with higher w_focus cannot recover the design.
applicability: All lens design runs using curriculum optimization with separable focus and aberration weights
Any run where EFL/F-number/FOV must stay within tight tolerances of target values
signals: EFL drift >50% from target after curriculum
LR ratio >10× between consecutive curriculum phases (increasing direction)
Spot RMS >1mm and MTF50 <5 cy/mm at any field
LR ratio >10× between consecutive phases (increasing direction) in curriculum or fine-tune
Fine-tune fails to recover specification drift from curriculum
guidance: Set w_focus ≥ 0.3 during curriculum to keep EFL/F-number/FOV anchored to targets
Ensure curriculum LR schedule is monotonically decreasing or flat; never increase LR by more than 5× between phases
Monitor specification drift after each curriculum phase; if drift exceeds 20%, raise w_focus before continuing
Consider starting with w_focus=0.5 and tapering aberration weights in, rather than keeping focus weight low
Ensure both curriculum and fine-tune LR schedules are monotonically decreasing or flat; never increase LR by more than 5× between phases
If curriculum drift exceeds 100%, restart with corrected weights rather than attempting fine-tune recovery
parameter_hints: w_focus ≥ 0.3 for curriculum; ≥ 0.5 recommended for first phase
LR schedule: monotonically decreasing, max 5× ratio between adjacent phases
weight_dropout ≤ 0.05 when w_focus is low to avoid further destabilization
anti_patterns: LR schedule with a mid-optimization spike (e.g., [..., 0.0001, 0.01, ...])
Assuming fine-tune phase can recover from >100% specification drift
w_focus=0.1 in curriculum with large FOV targets
100× LR increase between consecutive curriculum or fine-tune phases
Assuming fine-tune can recover from severe (>100%) curriculum drift
